tasks.subject: [community-owner-replacement] [P1] Let a Community host send notices by email through its own SMTP server
tasks.description:
Build optional outbound mail for apps/community, off by default, as specified in specs/community-owner-replacement/02-specification.md ("Mail delivery (new, optional)", "Technical Dependencies"). A replacement is refused without mail, so this comes first. Build order: after the host-operator import migration (0019) and the takedown migration (0020) are on main; take the next free migration number at build time and land one migration PR at a time.

Scope:
- Configuration in `src/config.ts`: `COMMUNITY_SMTP_URL` and `COMMUNITY_MAIL_FROM` (all or none; `smtps:` or STARTTLS required unless the host is loopback), `COMMUNITY_OWNER_REPLACEMENT_NOTICE_DAYS` (default 14, 7–90), `COMMUNITY_OWNER_REPLACEMENT_UNREACHABLE_DAYS` (default 30, 14–180, never below the notice days), `COMMUNITY_OWNER_REPLACEMENT_OBJECTION_COOLDOWN_DAYS` (default 90, 30–365). The startup log says whether mail is on, never the URL or credentials.
- `src/mail/transport.ts` (nodemailer, pinned exactly), `src/mail/outbox.ts` (queue inside the caller's transaction), `src/mail/worker.ts` (one message at a time per replica, SKIP LOCKED plus lease, existing cleanup backoff; `2xx` accepted; recipient `5xx` failed at once as `SMTP_REJECTED`; `4xx`/timeout/connection error retried until 72 hours after creation, then failed as `SMTP_UNAVAILABLE`; a recipient whose `"user"` row is gone or whose account erasure is open or done fails at once as `RECIPIENT_UNAVAILABLE` with nothing sent; `last_error_class` only), and a hook for a message kind to add per-send content (task 2.3 uses it to mint an object-only token per attempt; a failed attempt's token is never deleted, since a timeout may still deliver), `src/mail/messages.ts` (plain-text builder).
- The `notice_outbox` table in its own migration, mirrored in `src/schema.ts`, listed in `src/migrate.ts`; rows deleted 30 days after resolving and with the tenant by `deletion-worker.ts`. The address is never stored.
- `GET /api/v1/host/capabilities` (scope `communities:read`) → `{ mail, oidc }` with `CommunityAdminHostCapabilitiesSchema`.
- Docs: `DEPLOYMENT.md`, `README.md`, and `OPERATIONS.md` (setting up mail, and deliverability in generic terms: the sender domain in `COMMUNITY_MAIL_FROM` should pass SPF and DKIM and align under DMARC; watch failed notices; name no provider). Changelog fragment.

Acceptance criteria (real Postgres; `smtp-server` in process as a dev dependency; each test fails if the behaviour is removed or subtly wrong):
- AC-5 config bounds: `NOTICE_DAYS=6`, `UNREACHABLE_DAYS=13`, unreachable below notice, `OBJECTION_COOLDOWN_DAYS=29`, a plain non-loopback `smtp:` URL without STARTTLS, and only one of the two mail keys each fail `parseConfig`.
- With mail unset, the fake never receives a connection and capabilities says `mail: false`.
- Classification: 250 → accepted; 550 → failed `SMTP_REJECTED`; 421 repeatedly → retried with backoff, failed `SMTP_UNAVAILABLE` at 72 hours (clock injected); a hang → lease expiry and retry, and a concurrent `SELECT … FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` on the community row succeeds during the send; recipient row deleted, and recipient with an open account erasure → failed `RECIPIENT_UNAVAILABLE`, fake receives nothing.
- The outbox row never contains the address; `last_error_class` never contains reply text (sentinel scan).
- Two workers on one database deliver each message exactly once.
- `pnpm verify` green.

tasks.subject: [community-owner-replacement] [P2] Add the owner-replacement schemas, scope, and migration
tasks.description:
Add the wire contract and storage for specs/community-owner-replacement/02-specification.md ("Wire schemas", "Data model", "Scope and authority"). Build order: after the host-operator import migration (0019) and the takedown migration (0020) are on main; take the next free migration number at build time and land one migration PR at a time.

Scope:
- `packages/shared/src/community-admin-wire.ts`: reason (`owner_left_group`, `owner_unreachable`, `other`), state, request (reference `^[A-Za-z0-9 ._#-]{1,80}$`, no `:` or `/`), replacement (with `notice.verifiedAddress`, `wait`, `claimReissuedAt`, `cooldownUntil`, `claimantNamed`), create response, list, claim-token schemas; `communities:ownership` in `CommunityAdminHostApiKeyScopeSchema`, with the scope-array maximum one higher than main's at build time; `ownerReplacement` on `CommunityAdminHostProjectionSchema`.
- `packages/shared/src/community-wire.ts`: notice read (with owner `options`), objection, object-preflight, object, claim preflight, claim schemas and route constants; `NOTICE_DELIVERY_UNAVAILABLE`, `OWNER_REPLACEMENT_OPEN`, `OWNER_REPLACEMENT_COOLDOWN` in `CommunityWireErrorCodeSchema`. TSDoc on every export.
- One migration: `owner_replacements` (issuer and subject stored together, `after_objection`, `verified_address`, `claim_reissued_at`, every shape check, `UNIQUE (community_id, requested_by_host_actor, idempotency_key)`, the partial unique index on open states, the objected index, composite tenant foreign keys to `members(community_id,id)`); `owner_replacement_object_tokens`; `host_api_keys_scopes` gains `communities:ownership` and its cardinality ceiling grows by one over main's. Do **not** add the host audit `system` or tenant audit `host` actor kinds: the takedown migration (0020) adds both. Mirror in `src/schema.ts`; list in `src/migrate.ts`.
- `host-keys.js issue --scope communities:ownership`; the host page's scope checkbox (`HostApiKeys.tsx`).
- `deletion-worker.ts` deletes replacements and object tokens with the tenant.

Acceptance criteria:
- Schema tests: every strict schema refuses an extra field; the reference refuses `:`, `/`, `<`, a newline, and 81 characters; a scope array one longer than the new maximum is refused.
- Migration tests (real Postgres): two open rows for one community violate the partial index; a closed and an open row are allowed; the same idempotency key in two communities is allowed and twice in one is not; a `completed` row without `new_owner_member_id`, a closed row with a `claim_token_hash`, a subject without an issuer, and a `prior_owner_member_id` from another community each violate a check or foreign key; a key with an unknown scope, or more scopes than the new ceiling, is refused.
- The offline key command issues a working `communities:ownership` key.
- Existing tenancy and administration isolation suites pass unchanged. `pnpm verify` green.

tasks.subject: [community-owner-replacement] [P2] Let a host request, list, cancel, and reissue an owner replacement
tasks.description:
Build `src/routes/host-owner-replacements.ts` per specs/community-owner-replacement/02-specification.md ("Host routes", "Scope and authority", "Shared rules", "Audit").

Scope: `POST /host/communities/:id/owner-replacements` (scope `communities:ownership`; a person must send `password`, a key must not; SSO-only operators get `403 PASSWORD_REQUIRED` and must use a key; mail required; idempotency per community, actor, and key with payload hash; lifecycle `active`/`archived`/`held` and current `lifecycleVersion`; one open per community; cooling-off `409 OWNER_REPLACEMENT_COOLDOWN` within C days of the last objection; `after_objection` and `after_withdrawal` (a withdrawal within 30 days) recorded; with OIDC configured a subject is required (`400`) and stored with the configured issuer; without OIDC a subject is `409`; insert `notifying` row, claim-token hash, and one `owner_replacement.notice` message; audits per the table; `201`/`200`, `no-store`, `claimUrl` with the token in the fragment). `GET …/owner-replacements` (newest first, max 50, no member data, subject never echoed). `POST …/:replacementId/cancel` (open → `withdrawn`, tokens dead, `owner_replacement.ended` queued, no cooling-off). `POST …/:replacementId/claim-token` (reissue in an open state; dates unchanged; `claim_reissued_at` set; `owner_replacement.claim_reissued` email queued to the owner; audits on both planes). Host projection field. `assertHostActor` inside every write, community locked first.

Acceptance criteria (spec AC numbers):
- AC-1 scope, person reauthentication, SSO-only operator refused; AC-2 no mail, no replacement; AC-3 idempotency (including the same key in another community), one at a time, and a concurrent barrier producing one row.
- AC-7 (request half): with OIDC on a missing subject is `400`; the stored issuer equals the configured issuer; with OIDC off a subject is `409`.
- AC-10 (request half): refused in `pending_owner` (message names the claim reissue), `suspended`, `deletion_pending`; accepted in `active`, `archived`, `held`.
- AC-20 (request half): a request within C days of an objection is `409` with the end date; after C days it is accepted with `after_objection = true`; withdrawal, expiry, and supersession start no cooling-off.
- AC-21: reissue queues exactly one `claim_reissued` message, writes both audit rows, replaces the stored hash, and moves no date.
- A key revoked while its request waits on the community lock (test hook) fails `401` and writes nothing.
- AC-13 and AC-14 for these routes.
- Docs: `API.md` host section; `OPERATIONS.md` on naming an account (pairwise subject identifiers: use the subject the issuer gives this host), SSO-only operators using a key, and the defences said plainly: against a stolen key or a phished operator, on every host, the owner is protected by the notice, the wait, and the objection; the named identity only stops a stranger using a leaked claim link. `pnpm verify` green.

tasks.subject: [community-owner-replacement] [P2] Run the owner-replacement timeline, send the notices, and end it when the owner or host acts
tasks.description:
Build the timeline, the notices with object-only links, and the end hooks per specs/community-owner-replacement/02-specification.md ("Which wait applies", "Timeline worker", "Object-only link", "What the owner can actually do", "Things that end an open replacement", "Audit", and the email copy under "User Experience").

Scope:
- `src/owner-replacement/state.ts` (allowed transitions), `end.ts` (one helper that closes an open replacement inside the caller's transaction: state, `ended_at`, all tokens dead, audits per the table, `owner_replacement.ended` unless the owner acted; see below), `worker.ts` (notice resolution → `waiting` with `claimable_after` = resolved + N only for accepted mail to an address marked verified (by any sign-in service; the server never sets it), with `after_objection` and `after_withdrawal` false and a reason other than `owner_left_group`, else + U; the 48-hour reminder once; `claimable` with `claim_expires_at` = +14 days; `expired`), `options.ts` (keep always; transfer only in `active` with a password; delete only with a password), `object-tokens.ts` (mint one per send attempt through the 1.1 hook, hash at rest, never delete one when an attempt fails, single use, dead once the request closes).
- `src/mail/messages.ts`: notice, reminder, claim-reissued (each with an object-only link to `/keep-ownership#<token>`), ended (withdrawn, expired), and completed messages, minimal as the spec says (what is happening, the deadline, how to object), with the transfer and delete sentences only when `options.ts` allows them; UTC dates with the day spelled out; `/c/<uuid>` link; never a claim token, reason, reference, or legal-hold wording.
- Hooks: `POST /owner/transfer` and `POST /owner/deletion` → `superseded`; host `suspend`, host-started deletion, and the takedown's community deletion → `withdrawn` (beside the deletion-notice withdrawal in `host-lifecycle.ts`, and in the takedown route that is on main by then).

The end helper re-reads the replacement under the community lock: the owner_replacements row joined into `hostProjectionSql` by a `FOR UPDATE OF c` read (host-lifecycle.ts, owner-claims.ts) may be stale once the lock is granted. It also sets `withdrawn_cause` on a withdrawal and clears `claimant_oidc_issuer` and `claimant_oidc_subject` whenever a request closes (`claimant_named` stays).

Acceptance criteria:
- AC-4 the right wait: verified, accepted, `owner_unreachable` → N from acceptance; password-only account with accepted mail → U; `550` → U at once; 72 hours of `421` → U; with verified accepted mail, still U for a request after an objection, a request 29 days after a withdrawal (N at 31 days), and reason `owner_left_group`. Injected clocks.
- AC-9 (host and owner-action half): transfer (in `active`, with password), deletion request, suspension, host-started deletion, and cancel each close an open replacement in every open state, write the listed audits, and leave no live claim or object token.
- AC-15 mail content over every message kind, including the conditional transfer and delete sentences for each combination of lifecycle and password.
- AC-16 expiry after 14 days claimable, owner emailed, tokens dead.
- AC-19 (token half): tokens stored only as hashes; each notice, reminder, and reissue message carries a distinct live token; a send that times out after the fake accepted the body is retried and delivered again, and both delivered links still object (the first ends the request, the second answers the same success).
- The reminder is queued once, 48 hours before `claimable_after`, and never moves the date. A transition that races an objection or cancel (barrier) does nothing.
- AC-11 (timeline half); AC-13 for these transitions. Hold, release, archive, restore, limits, and short-name changes leave an open replacement untouched.
- `pnpm verify` green.

tasks.subject: [community-owner-replacement] [P2] Let the owner object and the named account take ownership, signing up if needed
tasks.description:
Build `src/routes/owner-replacement.ts` and the admission change per specs/community-owner-replacement/02-specification.md ("Object-only link", "Owner and member routes", "Claim and completion").

Scope: `GET /api/v1/communities/:communityId/owner-replacement` (owner sees the open request with reference and `options`; admins without reference or options; every member sees a completion for 7 days; bearer grants allowed for the DorkOS read). `POST …/owner-replacement/objection` (owner browser session only, bearer refused, no password; `active`/`archived`/`held`; idempotent). `POST /api/v1/owner-replacements/object-preflight` and `POST /api/v1/owner-replacements/object` (public, rate limited, token only, never a `GET`; one identical `403` for a dead token; replay after objection returns the same success with no second audit row). `POST /api/v1/owner-replacements/preflight` and `/claim` (signed 30-minute `community_owner_replacement` cookie; advisory lock distinct from owner claims; lock order community → replacement → members → user; `claimable` and before expiry; when no identity is named but the host now has OIDC configured, refuse `409` so the host asks again with a fresh wait; when an identity is named: configured issuer still equals the stored issuer, exactly one `account` row with `providerId='oidc'` and `accountId` = subject, and it is the session's; not the current owner; `memberIsLeaving` and `accountErasureOpen` refused; swap exactly as `/owner/transfer`; end the old owner's queued or building owner exports; audits; completed message). **Admission:** `checkAdmission` in `src/auth.ts` accepts a live cookie whose replacement is `claimable` and unexpired in an `active`/`archived`/`held` community; when an identity is named, only an OIDC sign-up through the configured issuer is admitted. Serve and reserve `/owner-replacement` and `/keep-ownership` in `main.ts` and `COMMUNITY_RESERVED_SHORT_NAMES`.

Acceptance criteria:
- AC-6 no early claim; AC-7 (claim half): a request with no identity whose host turned OIDC on before the claim is refused and changes nothing; no OIDC link, wrong subject, two matching account rows, and a changed issuer each refused with nothing changed and the cookie kept on `403`, the one right account succeeds; AC-8 completion equals transfer; AC-9 (objection half) including an SSO-only owner with no password, bearer refusal, admin refusal; AC-10 objection allowed in `held` while transfer stays refused; AC-12 erasure races (barrier); AC-17 tenant binding of claim and object tokens; AC-18 members told for 7 days and not before; AC-11 and AC-14 for these routes.
- AC-19 (route half): an object token objects without a session and starts the cooling-off; `GET` of the page and of the preflight changes nothing; the token is refused as a session, claim, grant, or on any other route; a withdrawn or expired request's token answers "This request has already ended."
- AC-22 sign-up through the claim: with a named subject, a person with no account signs up through the issuer with that subject and claims; a password sign-up with the same cookie is refused; a cookie for a `waiting`, expired, or objected request admits nobody; with OIDC off, a password sign-up with a live claimable cookie is admitted; without the cookie sign-up is refused as today.
- Two concurrent claims with one token produce exactly one completion (barrier). The reserved-name test still pins every top-level path.
- Docs: `API.md` tenant, object-link, and claim sections; `RECOVERY.md` says offline repair comes after the online path. Changelog fragment. `pnpm verify` green.

tasks.subject: [community-owner-replacement] [P3] Show the owner replacement in the Community browser app
tasks.description:
Build the browser surfaces per specs/community-owner-replacement/02-specification.md ("User Experience": host page, the object-only link page, owner, admins, every member, the new owner). All copy exactly as the spec, following `writing-for-humans`; "the account named in the request", never who asked.

Scope: `HostOwnerReplacement.tsx` in the host community record (the Replace the owner form with reason, reference, password for a person, and a required "Sign-in ID of the new owner" when OIDC is on; disabled with the mail sentence when `mail: false`, with the key sentence for an SSO-only operator, and with the cooling-off sentence during a cooling-off; one-time claim link reveal; each row's sentence for every state, including failed mail, the three long-wait reasons, expired, withdrawn with its cause, superseded, objected with the date the host may ask again; Cancel and Send the claim link again with the "owner will be told" confirm). `KeepOwnership.tsx` at `/keep-ownership` (reads the token from the fragment and clears it, preflights, one button, success and dead-link sentences; no action on load). `OwnerReplacementBanner.tsx` (owner version with Keep ownership and What this means, showing the reason sentence, the reference as quoted plain text, and only the options the notice read allows, plus the reissue line; admin version; member completion notice for 7 days, dismissible per browser with guarded storage access). `OwnerReplacementClaim.tsx` at `/owner-replacement` (fragment token, preflight, before-date and at-date states, sign in or sign up through the named sign-in service, Take ownership confirm, the five error sentences, Settings on success).

Acceptance criteria:
- Component tests per state and per row kind, each asserting the exact sentence and the route called (mock fetch); the reference renders as text, never an anchor, even when it looks like a domain.
- The owner banner shows the transfer sentence only for `active` with a password, the delete sentence only with a password, and the add-a-password sentence without one.
- Claim and object tokens never appear in `location.search`, a request URL, or console output (spy); fragments are cleared after preflight; loading `/keep-ownership` makes no objection request.
- Browser tests (`apps/community/browser-tests`) at phone and desktop widths: host form and every row state (including failed mail, expired, withdrawn, superseded, cooling-off), owner banner with each option combination, admin banner, the object-link page, the claim page before and after the date (clock control route), and the member notice; axe passes on each. `bash apps/community/acceptance/run.sh` green.
- Screenshots of each state eyeballed and attached to the PR.

tasks.subject: [community-owner-replacement] [P3] Tell the owner on their DorkOS connection
tasks.description:
Surface the owner's notice in the DorkOS app per specs/community-owner-replacement/02-specification.md ("User Experience": DorkOS app; "Performance Considerations").

Scope: the remote client in `apps/server/src/services/communities/remote/` reads `GET /api/v1/communities/:communityId/owner-replacement` with the connection's grant inside the existing per-connection read budget and caches it like the attention counts (a refusal clears it; a slow Community shows no notice rather than a stale one); the shared connection shape gains an optional owner notice; the client community row shows a warning dot and the community header shows the banner text with Open community; one notification when a request is first seen and one when it completes, only for the owner. Non-owners see nothing. Copy says only what this owner can do (from the notice read's `options`).

Acceptance criteria:
- Server tests with a fixture Community: an owner's connection gets the notice; an admin's and a member's do not; a `403` clears a cached notice; the budget is respected.
- Client tests with a mock Transport: warning dot and header text for an owner; nothing for a member; exactly one notification per request id across reloads.
- Dev Playground showcase for the row and header states if the component qualifies (`maintaining-dev-playground`).
- Changelog fragment; the Communities guide in `docs/` gains "If someone asks to take over your community", covering the email link for owners who can't sign in. `pnpm verify` green.
